Definition: from G575 and G138; to remove (literally or figuratively):--cut (smite) off, take away.
BiblicalUsage: To take away, to cut off — the Lord taking away Elizabeth's reproach, the servant's ear cut off in the garden, and the promise that God will take away sins. The word removes things: shame, an ear, and sin itself.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the best taking away in this word is the last one: God taking away sins is the promise the whole covenant stands on. Shame lifted, and sin removed: that is the taking away I live on.
